El ruido de gradiente sortea pendientes: Gradient noise draws slopes instead of values: it is 0 at the corners and avoids the chequered look of value noise.
El ruido de valor tiene un defecto que,: Value noise has a defect that, once seen, cannot be unseen: its maxima and minima fall exactly at the grid's corners, and the image has a chequered air. Ken Perlin avoided it by changing what is drawn at each corner. Instead of a value, a slope is drawn: a gradient vector. At the corner the noise is 0, but it leaves it with that inclination. Each corner contributes the [[ge-vectores|dot product]] of its gradient with the vector running from the corner to the point, and the four contributions are interpolated.
El ruido de valor tiene un solo tamaño d: Value noise has a single size of detail: patches all equally big. Real things are not like that. A mountain has big bumps, on those bumps there are medium bumps, on those there are stones and on the stones there is grain. El ruido fractal es, probablemente, la f: Fractal noise is, probably, the most profitable function in the history of graphics.
